procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 17.12.84 of the Gujarat High Court in Special Civil Application No. 2332 of 1984.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The appellant filed a writ petition under Art.226 challenging the validity of Rules 6(4)(i) and 6(4)(ii)(a), alleging that they were unreasonable, arbitrary, discriminatory and violating Articles 14 and 16. The High Court dismissed the petition holding that the age restriction provided by the recruiting authorities was valid.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The appellant appealed to the Supreme Court, reiterating the contentions raised in the High Court. The appeal was registered as Civil Appeal No. 2588 of 1985.

directions: The name of the appellant shall be deemed to have been continued in the select list of 1983-84 and his case for appointment to the post of Assistant Judge shall be considered on that basis by the authorities concerned.
If he is appointed to the post of Assistant Judge, he shall get his due seniority and all retiral benefits reckoning the service on that basis.

issue.issue_text: Whether rules 6(4)(i) and 6(4)(iii)(a) of the Gujarat Judicial Service Recruitment Rules 1961 as amended upto 1979 are invalid being arbitrary, irrational, unreasonable and in contravention of the equality clause envisaged in Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India.

law.law_text: Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution ensure that there should not be any discrimination in the matter of appointment in service, nor there will be any arbitrariness or unreasonableness in the rules of recruitment providing for appointment to the service either by promotion or by direct recruitment.

application.application_text: The Court found that there was no rationale or nexus to the object sought to be achieved by imposing an age restriction for promotion to the post of Assistant Judge. This was especially arbitrary because no such age limit existed for promotion to the higher post of a District Judge, even though both posts belong to the Senior Branch of the judicial service.

The Court found it incomprehensible how the two cadres of Assistant Judges and District Judges could be treated differently regarding age restrictions for promotion, deeming the distinction discriminatory.

The Court also noted that the rule was "archaic, unreasonable and irrational," pointing out that a similar rule that existed in the bilingual State of Bombay had since been deleted from the recruitment rules of the Maharashtra Judicial Service, yet was allowed to continue in Gujarat.

reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court decided that rules 6(4)(i) and 6(4)(iii)(a) were invalid because they were arbitrary, irrational, and discriminatory, thus violating the equality principles in Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution. The Court's reasoning was primarily based on the fact that the rules imposed an age restriction for promotion to the post of Assistant Judge, but not for the higher post of District Judge. The Court found no logical reason for this distinction, concluding that the rule was arbitrary and had no nexus to its intended objective. It also described the rule as "archaic" and noted that a similar provision had been removed in the neighboring state of Maharashtra.

arguments.issue_text: Whether rules 6(4)(i) and 6(4)(iii)(a) of the Gujarat Judicial Service Recruitment Rules 1961 as amended upto 1979 are invalid being arbitrary, irrational, unreasonable and in contravention of the equality clause envisaged in Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India.
appellant_arguments: The rules imposing an age restriction for promotion to the post of Assistant Judge are invalid as they are arbitrary, irrational, unreasonable, and violate the equality clauses in Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution.
respondent_arguments: There is a valid rationale behind imposing an age bar for the promotion to the post of Assistant Judge for persons already in service.

cases.principle: For the principle that Article 14 strikes at arbitrariness in State action and requires that State action must be based on a rational, relevant, and non-discriminatory principle, and not be guided by extraneous or irrelevant considerations.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution ensure that there shall be no discrimination in the matter of appointment in service, and that the rules of recruitment for appointment, whether by promotion or direct recruitment, must not be arbitrary or unreasonable.
obiter: The fixation of different ages of superannuation in different grades may be permissible in services such as the armed forces, air force, and naval force if it is in the public interest to ensure excellence, merit, and efficiency, which are highly dependent on physical fitness.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The provisions of rule 6(4)(i) and rule 6(4)(iii)(a) of the Gujarat Judicial Service Recruitment (amended rules), 1979 are invalid and bad as they are irrational, arbitrary and unreasonable inasmuch as there is no nexus to the object sought to be achieved by introducing the age restriction in regard to appointment of Assistant Judge by promotion from amongst members holding post of Civil Judges. This archaic, unreasonable and irrational rule is ex facie arbitrary and discriminatory.
legal_tests_applied: Reasonableness and rationality, which is legally as well as philosophically an essential element of equality or non-arbitrariness, is protected by Article 14 and it must characterise every State action.
policy_considerations: Fixation of different ages of superannuation may be permissible in public interest in services like the armed forces to ensure excellence and merit which depend on physical fitness, but this rationale does not apply to the judicial service.
